newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rates cut possible if liquidity high - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Thai rates cut possible if liquidity high - bankers.

text.p: Thai banks are likely to cut lending rates next month if money supply remains high and the overnight interbank rate remains at current low levels, the Thai Bankers Association said on Wednesday.

"If the (overnight) interbank rate stays at around 7.00-10.00 (percent) until the end of the month, there is a possibility that the lending rates of most commercial banks will be cut next month," Olarn Chaipravat, president of the Thai Bankers Association, told reporters after a luncheon.
Olarn, also president of Siam Commercial Bank Plc, said the current interbank rate of 7.00-10.00 percent was appropriate under the present economic conditions.
The Thai overnight interbank rate was at 7.50 percent in early morning from 7.00 percent late on Tuesday.
The financial system has been flush with liquidity in the past week, although it was slightly tighter on Wednesday because of value-added tax payments and heavy buying of the dollar, dealers said.
Thailand's lending rates are among the highest in the region and the minimum lending rate is around 13.25 percent.
